title: Shelly's Code Path
theme: A code path with symbols, finding and fixing the bug
blurb: Shelly the thirsty tortoise wants to get to the pond; Hoppy the rabbit lays out a code path of shape cards on the ground. But there's a “jump!” card in the code, and Shelly can't jump! The two friends find the mistake, fix the code and reach the pond by a new path.

pages.text: It was a hot summer's day. Shelly the tortoise was so thirsty. “I'll go to the pond for a drink!” he said. But the meadow grass was so tall. Shelly stretched his neck up, and up… No pond in sight! A big rock sat in the way. “Oh dear, which way now?”

tosbi.say: Where's the pond? I can't see it at all!

pages.ask: Why can't Shelly see the pond? How do you get to a place you can't see?

pages.text: Hop, hop! Hoppy the rabbit jumped up high. “The pond is over there! I'll make you a code path!” She laid cards on the ground. “Blue square: one step forward. Yellow star: jump!” The code was ready: square, square, star, square.

zipzip.say: The pond's over there! Follow the code, Shelly!

pages.ask: What shapes are on the cards? What does the blue square mean? And the yellow star?

pages.text: Shelly followed the code. Square: one step. Square: one more step. Now it was the star's turn. “Jump? But I can't jump!” Shelly stood stuck in front of the rock. He was so cross. “Humph! This code is broken!”

zipzip.say: Hmm… There's a mistake in the code!

predict.q: What do you think they'll do now?
predict.res: Both are good ideas! Let's see.

pages.ask: Why did Shelly stop? How do you feel when a plan doesn't work?

pages.text: Hoppy scratched her ear. “My mistake! I made the code for a rabbit.” Shelly took a deep breath. “I can't jump, but I can go around!” They took the star away and put a red circle in its place. Circle: go around the rock!

mech.done: Code done: square, square, circle, square!

pages.hint: Read the new code in order!
pages.ask: What did Hoppy do when she made a mistake? How do you fix a mistake?

pages.text: Shelly followed the new code. Square: plod, plod, one step. Square: one more step. Circle: around the rock he went. Last square: one more step. Hoppy clapped: “The code works!” The pond was right under Shelly's nose.

tosbi.say: Plod, plod, I'm following the code!

mech.done: The code works! Shelly reached the pond.

pages.ask: Which cards took Shelly to the pond? Can you say the cards in order?

pages.text: Glug, glug! Shelly drank and drank the cool water. “Ahh, lovely!” he said. Hoppy hopped on the bank: “My first code was broken, wasn't it?” Shelly laughed: “Never mind! If it breaks, we fix it. If one way doesn't work, we find another way!”

tosbi.say: Glug, glug! If it breaks, we fix it!

zipzip.say: Let's make a new code tomorrow!

pages.ask: If you made a code path, what shapes would you put on your cards? What would each shape mean?

kazanim: MAB.3 Interpreting mathematical facts, events and objects — process component MAB.3.a: expresses mathematical facts and events with different materials and symbols. Shows movements with shape cards (blue square = one step forward, red circle = go around) and reads the sequence of cards in order.
KB3.2 Problem Solving: finds where the code does not work (a “jump” card for a tortoise that cannot jump), removes the wrong card, puts a suitable one in its place and tries the code again.
skill: SBAB7 Spatial Thinking — describes and follows a path using position and direction words such as forward, in front of, around, towards the pond.

SDB3.2 Flexibility: when the plan does not work, stops, breathes and changes the plan, saying “If one way doesn't work, we find another way.” Value: D3 Diligence — does not give up when the first code breaks; looks for the mistake, changes the card and tries the code again.
once: Point to the tortoise and the rabbit on the cover: “The rabbit hops; what does the tortoise do? Can they both go the same way in the same manner?”

Explain the word “code”: “Signs that tell someone what to do, in order, are called a code. If I draw a square and say ‘This means one step forward’, can you make me walk?” Try a tiny two-step code in the room.
sirasi: On page 1, talk about why Shelly can't see the pond: “Shelly is down on the ground, the grass is tall. What does Hoppy see when she jumps?”

On page 2, touch the cards one by one; say together what each card says: square, square, star, square. If the child spots the mistake straight away, say “Let's see what Shelly does!” and keep them waiting.
On page 3, name Shelly's frustration: “His plan didn't work, he's upset.” At the prediction question, accept both answers; both are good solutions.
On page 4, let the child read the new code in order. Point out Hoppy saying “My mistake”: making mistakes and fixing them are both normal.
On page 5, say the name of the card at every touch of Shelly: “Square… square… circle… square!” If the child likes, they can do the steps on the spot themselves.
On page 6, say the sentence “If it breaks, we fix it” together, with rhythm; the child tells about a time they fixed their own mistake.
sonra: Why didn't the first code work? What did Shelly and Hoppy change?
What did Shelly do when he was upset? What do you do when something doesn't work out?
If we made a code for Hoppy, which card could we use? And which one for Shelly?
Put the three pictures from the story in the order the events happened: first, next, last.

sinif.materyal: Blue squares, red circles and yellow stars cut from card; a “rock” placed on the floor (a cushion or a box); a “pond” at the end of the path (blue fabric or paper)
adim: Choose the meaning of the cards together and hang them on the board as pictures: blue square = one step forward, red circle = go around the obstacle, yellow star = jump or another movement the children choose.

One child is the “coder” and lays the cards on the floor; another child is “Shelly” and reads the cards in order and walks. A friend who uses a wheelchair can move along the same code too; everyone does the movement in their own way.
The teacher deliberately puts one card wrong; the children read the code card by card asking “Where's the mistake?”, find it and fix it.
To close, swap roles; give each child a chance to be the coder once and the walker once. Finish with the question “What do we do if the code breaks?”

evSoru: In Hoppy's first code, which card didn't suit Shelly?
Which card did they put in place of the star? What did that card mean?
What do you do when a plan of yours doesn't work out?

evEtk.d: Cut a few squares and circles out of paper. In the living room, pick a toy as the target and make obstacles with cushions. Your child lays the cards on the floor and “codes” you to the target; you follow the cards in order. Now and then, deliberately follow a card wrongly or lay a wrong card; your child finds the mistake and fixes the code.

guide.aileNotu: Today we read “Shelly's Code Path.” Hoppy the rabbit laid out a code of shape cards on the ground to get Shelly the tortoise to the pond; but she had put a “jump” card in the code that Shelly couldn't do. The two friends found the mistake, changed the card and reached the pond with the new code. Our children practised building a sequence of steps with symbols, finding and fixing a mistake, and being flexible when a plan doesn't work. At home you can play with simple card codes and use the sentence “If it breaks, we fix it” together.
